claims.text: An active-learning moment tensor potential trained on diversified, uncertainty-quantified data will enable accurate ab initio-level free-energy evaluations for both solid and liquid high-entropy alloys.
The proposed framework will substantially reduce the computational cost of obtaining fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties.
Training and calibration will begin with elemental and binary systems before extension to CoCrFeNi-based high-entropy alloys.
The training configurations will represent both solid and liquid states near the melting point.
Active learning will identify high-uncertainty regions, especially configurations spanning the phase transition.
Adding targeted high-fidelity ab initio data in high-uncertainty regions will ensure accurate critical free-energy and entropy contributions.
The intended temperature domain is approximately 0.8Tm to 1.1Tm.
Local-environment and short-range-order descriptors can represent relevant structural differences between the solid and liquid phases.
Active-learning uncertainty metrics can monitor and guide refinement of potential accuracy across the two phases.
Reproducing ab initio forces and energies with an ML-MTP inherently captures vibrational entropy.
Reproducing ab initio forces and energies with an ML-MTP inherently captures anharmonicity.
Reproducing ab initio forces and energies with an ML-MTP inherently captures electron–vibration coupling.
Iteratively adding ab initio data wherever the model is uncertain will maintain accuracy across the solid–liquid transition.
The framework will produce phase free-energy curves and melting properties with fidelity comparable to full ab initio molecular dynamics.
The framework will produce phase free-energy curves and melting properties with fidelity comparable to TOR-TILD.
The proposed framework will provide a 10–50× speedup.
The efficiency gain will make the method scalable to compositionally complex high-entropy alloys.
Explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows and TOR-TILD achieve high accuracy but have significantly higher computational costs.
Transferability to extreme configurations near the phase transition is a key uncertainty.
